title: Check the identity of someone representing HMRC in person
text:
Contact in person

 Anyone representing HMRC will always identify themselves and explain why they are visiting you.

 If you’re unsure about whether the person you are dealing with is a genuine HMRC officer, you can contact HMRC to check their identity and confirm they are an officer from HMRC.

 Confirming an HMRC officer’s identity

 The officer will show you their HMRC identification card, which includes their name, photograph and HMRC serial number.

 • Make a note of the officer’s name and serial number.

 • The officer will give you an HMRC telephone number (03000 565 656) to call.

 • Call the number and give the HMRC adviser the officer’s name and serial number.

 • The adviser will confirm whether the person is a genuine HMRC officer.

 The telephone number provided by the HMRC officer:

 • is available 24 hours a day

 • is only for verifying the identity of HMRC officers in face to face situations

 • cannot help with queries about emails, letters or phone calls you have received from HMRC

 You should not use this telephone number to contact HMRC for general enquiries.

 If you do have a general enquiry you can  contact HMRC .

 Confirming an HMRC collector’s identity

 An HMRC collector will usually visit you between 8am to 6pm, Monday to Friday.

 If a collector visits you at any other time and you want to confirm their identity, arrange an appointment with them to return between 8am and 6pm, Monday to Friday.

 The collector will show you their HMRC identification card which will have their name, photograph and HMRC serial number on it.

 • Make a note of the name and serial number on the card.

 • Phone HMRC on 0300 200 3862.

 • Give the name and serial number to the adviser, so they can confirm that the collector represents HMRC.

 Find out about call charges .

 Get more information

 You can  check a list of genuine HMRC contacts  to help you decide if any contact you have received is from HMRC, or is a scam from a fraudster.

 Report suspicious HMRC emails, texts, social media accounts and phone calls

 Contact HMRC to report a suspicious email, social media account, phone call or text message that mentions HMRC.
